common_name: Decadence Vanilla Cream II Baptisia (Re-Blooming Creamy Yellow-White False Indigo)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained, average-to-poor soil in full sun to part sun, choosing a permanent site since Baptisia develops a deep taproot and resents transplanting once established; Vanilla Cream II is a re-blooming Decadence-series hybrid (US Plant Patent USPP 36,762).

directions: Plant in average to poor, well-drained soil in full sun to part sun (at least four hours of direct light), siting it permanently since Baptisia forms a deep taproot and does not transplant or divide well once established. Vanilla Cream II is an improved successor to the original Vanilla Cream, bred for a branching habit on dark charcoal-colored stems that produces creamy yellow-white, pea-like flowers over a longer season, with a second and sometimes third flush of bloom following the initial late-spring display rather than a single flush. It is drought-tolerant, salt-tolerant, deer-resistant, attractive to pollinators, and essentially maintenance-free once established, needing only an occasional late-winter cutback for tidiness.
